claims.claim: After cyclically orienting both Hamilton cycles, the coefficient B in the directed product satisfies B=Σ_H(-1)^|H|, where H ranges over arc subsets with indegree_H(v)=outdegree_H(v) at every vertex; the requested A equals ±B.
claims.evidence: Each vertex is the tail of two directed arcs, so division by ∏_v x_v² gives ∏_{u→v}(1-x_v/x_u). A selected arc set H contributes sign (-1)^|H| and exponent indegree_H(v)-outdegree_H(v), hence contributes to the constant term exactly when balanced. Reorienting any occurrence negates its factor, producing only one overall sign between A and B. Exact enumeration confirmed this on all 16 cycle pairs through n=5.
claims.search_method: Direct algebraic coefficient extraction, followed by exhaustive exact-integer comparison.

claims.claim: Let T be a nonempty even vertex set. Call T compatible when the two cyclic orders induce the same alternating bipartition of T, up to swapping its two classes. Then B=(1+(-1)^n)^2+2Σ_T w(T), where the sum is over compatible T and w(T)∈{±1} is well-defined.
claims.evidence: Writing a_i(v) for the selected outgoing arc of cycle i, balance is a_1(v)-a_1(pred_1v)=-(a_2(v)-a_2(pred_2v)). Thus both binary strings switch at the same even set T, in opposite directions. Switch directions alternate around each cycle, giving exactly the stated compatibility condition. Every compatible nonempty T yields two simultaneous-complement solutions; their sizes have equal parity because there are 2n arcs. For T empty the four constant-string pairs sum to (1+(-1)^n)^2. Exhaustive enumeration confirmed the classification and signs through n=5.
claims.search_method: Binary switch-equation proof and exhaustive balanced-subset enumeration.

claims.claim: If N_n is the number of compatible nonempty sets, then E[N_n]=Σ_{1<=k<=n/2} binom(n,2k)/binom(2k-1,k), this expectation has exponential growth rate 3/2, and E|A_n|<=4+2E[N_n].
claims.evidence: For fixed |T|=2k, after fixing one element of one alternating class, there are (2k-1)! induced cyclic orders and k!(k-1)! alternating orders, so compatibility has probability 1/binom(2k-1,k). Linearity gives the formula. If q=2k/n, the logarithmic rate of a summand is H(q)-q log 2+o(1), uniquely maximized at q=1/3 with value log(3/2); polynomially many summands do not alter the rate. Claim 1 gives |A_n|≤4+2N_n. Exact averaging over every second cycle through n=7 matched the formula.
claims.search_method: Exact cyclic-order counting, entropy maximization, and exhaustive rational averaging.

claims.claim: For min-label-oriented edge occurrences, A_n=(-1)^n Σ_c s(c), where c ranges over proper 3-colorings and s(c)=∏_{u<v} ε_c(u,v), with ε_c(u,v)=+1 if c(v)-c(u)=1 mod 3 and -1 otherwise.
claims.evidence: Third-root filtering isolates exponent 2 because every variable exponent lies in {0,…,4}. Improper colorings vanish. For proper edges, ζ^a-ζ^b=(ζ-ζ²)ε(a,b)ζ^{-(a+b)}. Degree four cancels all color phases, while (ζ-ζ²)^{2n}/3^n=(-1)^n. Direct coefficient extraction and the coloring sum agreed for all 436 cycle pairs through n=7.
claims.search_method: Exact root-of-unity filter and exhaustive integer comparison.

claims.claim: The S_3 action on proper colorings is free and preserves s(c). Consequently A_n is divisible by 6 and A_n/6=(-1)^n(N_+-N_-), where N_± count positive and negative color-orbits. In particular, an odd total number of color-orbits forces A_n≠0.
claims.evidence: Color rotations preserve every edge sign. A reflection reverses all 2n edge-occurrence signs and hence preserves their product. Every proper coloring uses at least two colors, so no nonidentity color permutation fixes it and every orbit has size six. Summing Claim 3 by orbits proves the formula and divisibility; N_+-N_- has the same parity as N_++N_-, proving the final implication.
claims.search_method: Direct analysis of the six global color permutations.

claims.claim: Three-colorability alone does not force nonvanishing: for C1=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7) and C2=(1,4,5,3,6,7,2), the graph has 12 proper 3-colorings but A_7=0.
claims.evidence: Exact enumeration found precisely 12 proper colorings. Fixing c(1)=0,c(2)=1 leaves exactly the two stated representatives, whose signs are +1 and -1; their six-element orbits cancel. Independent direct polynomial coefficient propagation also returned A_7=0.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of all 3^7 colorings plus independent exact coefficient propagation.
claims.witness: C1=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7), C2=(1,4,5,3,6,7,2); normalized orbit representatives (0,1,0,1,2,1,2) and (0,1,2,1,0,1,2) have respective signs +1 and -1, and the direct coefficient is 0.

claims.claim: If C1=C2 as undirected cycles, then A_n=(-1)^n(2^n+2(-1)^n), so A_n is nonzero for every n>=3.
claims.evidence: Every edge occurs twice, so every edge sign in Claim 3 squares to one. The signed sum is therefore the number of proper 3-colorings of C_n, namely 2^n+2(-1)^n. This is positive for n≥3. Direct coefficient extraction verified the displayed values for every 3≤n≤12.
claims.search_method: Reduction to the chromatic polynomial of a cycle and exact coefficient checks.

claims.claim: For the random model, after fixing C1 by relabeling there is a fixed vector f∈{0,±1}^{3^n} and uniform π∈S_n such that |A_n|=|X_π| for X_π=<f,U_πf>, and ||f||²=q_n=2^n+2(-1)^n.
claims.evidence: Conditional relabeling makes C1 canonical and leaves C2 uniform. A uniform coordinate permutation produces every directed Hamilton cycle equally often; forgetting direction produces the required uniform undirected cycle. With f the signed proper-coloring indicator of the canonical directed cycle, the two-cycle signed sum is its permuted inner product. Cycle reversal and conversion to min-label orientations change only an overall sign. Its squared norm counts proper cycle colorings and equals q_n. All 436 cycle pairs through n=7 satisfied the absolute-value identity, and q_n was checked through n=8.
claims.search_method: Group-action representation followed by exhaustive exact comparison.

claims.claim: The signed color-count generating polynomial is F_n(z_0,z_1,z_2)=tr((diag(z)W)^n); it is zero for odd n and equals 2(-1)^k(z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2)^k for n=2k.
claims.evidence: The trace expansion is exactly the cyclic-word signed generating function. For M=diag(z)W, det(λI-M)=λ(λ²+S), where S=z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2. Newton identities therefore give tr(M^{2k+1})=0 and tr(M^{2k})=2(-S)^k. Exhaustive integer coefficient dictionaries agreed for every 3≤n≤10.
claims.search_method: Formal characteristic-polynomial calculation and exhaustive symbolic-coefficient enumeration.

claims.claim: For even n=2k, if m_n=E_π[X_π], then m_n=4Σ_{p+q+r=k} binom(k;p,q,r)^2/binom(2k;p+q,p+r,q+r), and Pr[A_n≠0]>=m_n/(2^n+2)>=4/(2^n+2). Moreover m_n tends to 16/3.
claims.evidence: Projection onto coordinate-count classes gives m_n=Σ_α S_α²/binom(2k;α); substituting Claim 8 yields the exact sum. Cauchy-Schwarz against the constant vector gives m_n≥F_n(1,1,1)²/3^{2k}=4, while |X_π|≤q_n gives m_n≤q_n Pr[X_π≠0]. For the limit, with x=(p,q,r)/k the entropy exponent is 2(H(x)-H(Dx)), where Dx=((x_p+x_q)/2,(x_p+x_r)/2,(x_q+x_r)/2). Strict entropy concavity gives the unique maximum at (1/3,1/3,1/3). In two local coordinates the negative Hessian is [[9,9/2],[9/2,9]], with determinant 243/4, and Stirling's prefactor is 3√3/(πk). The resulting discrete Gaussian sum tends to 4/3 before the outer factor 4, hence m_n→16/3; the compact tail is exponentially negligible by the strict entropy gap. Exact enumeration matched the mean formula through n=8, with additional exact-rational evaluations through k=40.
claims.search_method: Invariant projection, exact rational summation, and a discrete Laplace/Stirling analysis with explicit Hessian and prefactor.

claims.evidence: For h=f⊗f, averaging the diagonal coordinate action is an orthogonal projection P, so E[X_π²]=||Ph||². For every σ∈S_3 and color-count vector α, the coordinate-pair orbit {(c,σc)} contributes N_α²/binom(n;α). These six families are disjoint because a proper cyclic word uses at least two colors. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives Σ_α N_α²/binom(n;α)≥q_n²/3^n, and multiplication by six proves the bound. Exact second moments through n=8 satisfied it.
claims.search_method: Orthogonal-projection decomposition by exact contingency-table orbits, plus exhaustive moment checks.

claims.evidence: Cauchy-Schwarz gives |X_π|≤||f||²=q_n, hence X_π²≤q_n²·1_{X_π≠0}. Combining expectations with Claim 10 and using equality of the zero events yields the stated bound. Exact probabilities through n=8 also satisfied it.
claims.search_method: Deterministic norm bound combined with the verified second-moment inequality and exact enumeration.

claims.claim: Using the a.a.s. 3-colorability result quoted in the supplied source, Pr[A_n=0]=Pr[N_+=N_->0]+o(1). Thus the unresolved target is precisely anti-concentration of the signed color-orbit imbalance.
claims.evidence: Claim 4 gives A_n=0 exactly when N_+=N_-. On a non-3-colorable graph both counts are zero; on a 3-colorable graph equality forces both to be positive. These cases partition the zero event. The quoted a.a.s. 3-colorability result makes the first case o(1), proving the probability identity and the stated equivalence.
claims.search_method: Exact event decomposition using the orbit formula and the asymptotic premise explicitly quoted in the source.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a proof that Pr[A_n≠0] tends to one or a proof that this limit assertion is false. The draft proves neither. Its lower bounds 6·3^{-n} and, for even n, at least 4/(2^n+2), both decay; the n=7 cancellation witness does not determine an asymptotic limit; and the compatible-set and signed-coloring reformulations leave the required anti-concentration unresolved. These are nevertheless correct, material structural and finite-n advances. The final writeup explicitly disclaims resolution and labels itself PARTIAL, so the claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated.
